tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

# Discovery pipeline — FUS-enabled drug repurposing

Owner: Jeremy. Status: **scripted demo built** on `main`
(`frontend/src/components/discovery/`, `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts`).

Recorded 2026-11-07 from Jeremy's pitch, plus what's actually in the code.
Where the two differ, the code wins and this file says so.

---

## 1. The pitch

> The blood–brain barrier was the biggest barrier to drug delivery for ALS.
> With focused-ultrasound MRI from Sunnybrook, we can now look into new drugs
> that couldn't penetrate the BBB that can potentially reduce symptoms,
> develop a cure, or increase life expectancy.

**The move is an inversion.** Every repurposing screen for a CNS disease
treats BBB permeability as a filter and throws away what can't cross. If
MRgFUS can open the barrier focally and temporarily, that discarded set
becomes the interesting one — it has been excluded on a delivery constraint,
not on biology.

This is the strongest framing the project has had, because the thing it
proposes to search is a set nobody has had a reason to search.

### It connects to work already in this repo

`data/pipeline.json` carries a **graveyard partition**: every drug that
failed a human ALS trial, split into

- `never_arrived` — predicted barrier-negative, so it may never have reached
  the tissue at the dose that mattered, and
- `arrived_failed` — predicted barrier-positive, got there, still failed.

**`never_arrived` is, by construction, the candidate pool this pitch is

content.content:
/**
 * Addo Labs discovery pipeline: types, a sample patient, and a SCRIPTED run.
 *
 *   1. Patient analysis agent  (NCBI / ClinVar / Open Targets tool calls)
 *   2. 5 profile agents in parallel, each writing a slightly different ideal-drug profile
 *   3. DRKG embedding: each profile → TransE vector → cosine search over compounds
 *   4. Research agent (open web search) ranks candidates for THIS patient on
 *      fit, safety/interactions, cost, availability/regulation, acceptance
 *   5. Cited report
 *
 * `runDemoPipeline` replays fixed events on timers, the way Callio Labs' demo
 * sequence does. A live backend only has to emit the same `PipelineEvent`s.
 * All outputs below are ILLUSTRATIVE — the UI labels the run "Simulated".
 */

export type StageId = 'analysis' | 'profiles' | 'embedding' | 'research' | 'report'

export const STAGES: { id: StageId; label: string; detail: string }[] = [
  { id: 'analysis', label: 'Patient analysis', detail: 'NCBI · ClinVar · Open Targets' },
  { id: 'profiles', label: '5 profile agents', detail: 'Ideal-drug profiles, in parallel' },
  { id: 'embedding', label: 'DRKG embedding', detail: 'Cosine search over compounds' },
  { id: 'research', label: 'Research agent', detail: 'Open search · patient-specific ranking' },
  { id: 'report', label: 'Report', detail: 'Cited, exportable' },
]

export type AgentStep = {
  type: 'thinking' | 'tool_call' | 'tool_result' | 'output'
  label: string
  content: string
}

export type Patient = {
  id: string
  label: string
  age: number
  sex: string
  onset: string
  monthsSinceDx: number
  alsfrs: number
  slope: number // points / month
  fvc: number // % predicted
  genetics: string
  medications: string[]
  comorbidities: string[]
  location: string
  coverage: string
  preferences: string[]
  fusEligible: boolean
}

export const SAMPLE_PATIENT: Patient = {
  id: 'A-0417',
  label: 'Patient A-0417',
  age: 58,
  sex: 'F',
  onset: 'Bulbar onset',
  monthsSinceDx: 14,
  alsfrs: 38,
  slope: -0.9,
  fvc: 72,
  genetics: 'Panel negative (SOD1, C9orf72, FUS, TARDBP)',
  medications: ['Riluzole 50 mg BID', 'Edaravone (oral)', 'Lisinopril 10 mg'],
  comorbidities: ['Hypertension', 'CKD stage 2'],
  location: 'Toronto, ON, Canada',
  coverage: 'OHIP + private drug plan',
  preferences: ['Open to clinical trials', 'Prefers outpatient care', 'Avoids daily injections if possible'],
  fusEligible: true,
}

export type DrugProfile = {
  lane: number
  name: string
  hypothesis: string
  targets: string[]
  modality: string
  constraints: string[]
}

export const PROFILES: DrugProfile[] = [
  {
    lane: 0,
    name: 'Neurotrophic rescue',
    hypothesis: 'Support surviving upper and lower motor neurons with growth-factor signalling.',
    targets: ['IGF1R', 'RET (GDNF)', 'NTRK2 (BDNF)'],
    modality: 'Recombinant protein · ≤ 150 kDa',
    constraints: ['BBB not required (MRgFUS)', 'No hypoglycaemia-prone co-medication'],
  },
  {
    lane: 1,
    name: 'Cytokine neuroinflammation',
    hypothesis: 'Dampen microglial and astrocytic IL-6 / IL-1 signalling in motor cortex.',
    targets: ['IL6R', 'IL1R1', 'TNF'],
    modality: 'Monoclonal antibody / receptor antagonist',
    constraints: ['Infection risk acceptable with monitoring', 'Renal dosing compatible with CKD 2'],
  },
  {
    lane: 2,
    name: 'Complement blockade',
    hypothesis: 'Interrupt complement-mediated synapse and neuromuscular-junction loss.',
    targets: ['C5', 'C3', 'C1QA'],
    modality: 'Monoclonal antibody',
    constraints: ['Requires meningococcal vaccination', 'Infusion schedule'],
  },
  {
    lane: 3,
    name: 'TDP-43 proteostasis',
    hypothesis: 'Clear cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregates via autophagy enhancement.',
    targets: ['TARDBP', 'MTOR', 'TFEB'],
    modality: 'Small molecule or ASO',
    constraints: ['Sporadic ALS: TDP-43 pathology expected', 'Avoid immunosuppression stacking'],
  },
  {
    lane: 4,
    name: 'Excitotoxicity & oxidative stress',
    hypothesis: 'Reduce glutamate excitotoxicity and oxidative damage beyond current therapy.',
    targets: ['SLC1A2 (EAAT2)', 'GRIA2', 'NFE2L2 (NRF2)'],
    modality: 'Small molecule',
    constraints: ['Must not duplicate riluzole / edaravone', 'No CYP1A2 inhibition'],
  },
]

export type Match = { drug: string; lane: number; cosine: number; x: number; y: number; note?: string }

/** Top DRKG neighbours per profile, with a 2D projection for the embedding plot. */

import json
import os
import threading
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from server import bbb_adapter
from server.presets import PRESETS

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PIPELINE = Path(os.environ.get("PIPELINE_PATH", ROOT / "data" / "pipeline.json"))

app = FastAPI(title="ALS repurposing connector")
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origin_regex=r"http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)(:\d+)?",
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)
_cache = {"mtime": None, "data": None}
_warm = {"done": False}


def read_pipeline():
    if not PIPELINE.exists():
        raise HTTPException(503, f"{PIPELINE.name} not found; run merge or use sample.")
    mt = PIPELINE.stat().st_mtime
    if _cache["mtime"] != mt:
        _cache["data"] = json.loads(PIPELINE.read_text())
        _cache["mtime"] = mt
    return _cache["data"]


@app.on_event("startup")
def warm():
    def run():
        for p in PRESETS:
            if p.get("smiles"):
                try:
                    bbb_adapter.predict(p["smiles"])
                except Exception:
                    pass
        _warm["done"] = True

    threading.Thread(target=run, daemon=True).start()


@app.get("/api/health")
def health():
    return {"ok": True, "pipeline_present": PIPELINE.exists(), "bbb_model_wired": bbb_adapter.model_available(), "warm": _warm["done"]}


@app.get("/api/pipeline")
def pipeline():
    return read_pipeline()


@app.get("/api/presets")
def presets():
    return {"presets": PRESETS}


class PredictBody(BaseModel):
    smiles: str = Field(min_length=1)


@app.post("/api/predict")
def predict(body: PredictBody):
    try:
        return bbb_adapter.predict(body.smiles)
    except bbb_adapter.InvalidSmiles as e:
        raise HTTPException(422, str(e))
----
"""DRKG loading, and the one piece of knowledge everything downstream depends on:
which node and which relation actually represent "treats ALS".

Do not guess the ALS node. DRKG entity ids carry no names, so grepping the entity
list for "amyotrophic" returns nothing - you have to grep for the ontology ids and
then count the edges. Run this module to redo that check from scratch:

    python -m src.drkg

It prints the report and writes artifacts/als_node.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
from typing import Iterator

import numpy as np

from src.paths import ARTIFACTS, RAW, ensure_dirs

DRKG_URL = "https://dgl-data.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/dataset/DRKG/drkg.tar.gz"

TRIPLES = RAW / "drkg.tsv"
EMBED_DIR = RAW / "embed"
ENTITIES_TSV = EMBED_DIR / "entities.tsv"
RELATIONS_TSV = EMBED_DIR / "relations.tsv"
ENTITY_EMB = EMBED_DIR / "DRKG_TransE_l2_entity.npy"
RELATION_EMB = EMBED_DIR / "DRKG_TransE_l2_relation.npy"

# Confirmed by edge count, not by assumption. See module docstring and
# artifacts/als_node.json. MeSH D000690 is amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
ALS_NODE = "Disease::MESH:D000690"

# Candidates checked when resolving the ALS node. DOID:332 is also ALS, but it is a
# near-orphan in DRKG; D016472 is motor neuron disease, the parent term.
ALS_CANDIDATES = [
    "Disease::MESH:D000690",
    "Disease::DOID:332",
    "Disease::OMIM:105400",
    "Disease::MESH:D016472",
]

# The three relations DRKG uses for "a compound treats a disease". They come from
# different sources and - critically - they do not share a disease namespace.
TREATS_RELATIONS = [
    "DRUGBANK::treats::Compound:Disease",
    "GNBR::T::Compound:Disease",
    "Hetionet::CtD::Compound:Disease",
]

# The relation we score the missing edge with. GNBR::T carries 55 of the 57 existing
# treats edges on the ALS node, so it is the one the embedding actually learned.
SCORING_RELATION = "GNBR::T::Compound:Disease"


----
"""Component A. Score every compound for the missing Compound-treats-ALS edge, and
produce a short typed path to ALS as the receipt the UI displays.

    python -m src.kg_rank

Writes data/kg_scores.json.

Method
------
Pretrained DRKG TransE_l2 embeddings, 400 dimensions. We do not train our own model;
that is the first item on the cut list and the pretrained vectors give a ranked list in
seconds.

TransE embeds a triple so that head + relation ~= tail, so the plausibility of the
missing edge is the negative distance between where the compound lands after the
relation translation and where ALS actually sits:

    score(c) = gamma - || e_c + e_treats - e_ALS ||_2

gamma = 12.0, the margin DGL-KE used to train these vectors. It is a constant, so it
shifts every score equally and changes no ranking; it is kept only so the numbers read
on the same scale as the published DRKG repurposing example.

Honesty note that belongs on the judging slide
----------------------------------------------
Riluzole (DB00740) and edaravone (DB12243) already have treats edges to the ALS node in
DRKG, so they were in the data these embeddings were fit on. Their ranks are a sanity
check that the scoring function is wired up correctly, not a held-out evaluation. The
module labels them `in_training_graph: true` and reports an additional rank computed over
compounds that have no existing ALS treats edge, which is the honest comparison.

Paths
-----
`data/kg_scores.json` carries a 2-3 hop typed path to ALS for the top 100, found by BFS
over a relation-filtered subgraph.

The spec asks for drug -> target gene -> pathway -> ALS. **That path does not exist in
DRKG**: there are 84,372 Gene-Pathway edges but zero Pathway-Disease edges, so a pathway
can never be the last hop before ALS. The reachable shapes, in the order we prefer them:

1. compound -> gene -> ALS                     (2 hops, gene is an ALS-associated gene)
2. compound -> gene -> gene -> ALS             (3 hops, via a gene-gene interaction)
3. compound -> gene -> pathway -> gene -> ALS  (4 hops, the pathway-mediated receipt)

Shape 3 is emitted only when 1 and 2 fail, because DRKG pathway nodes are Pathway Commons
`PC7_*` ids with no name available offline - fine as structure, poor as a UI label.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

----
# Patient-constrained drug repurposing for ALS

**BioHacks 2026.** Rank approved drugs against ALS biology, then disqualify
the ones that are unsafe or unusable for one specific patient.

Most repurposing work stops at "this drug plausibly treats this disease". This
asks the next question: *can this person actually take it?* The constraints
come from a chart — what he can swallow, what his breathing tolerates, what
collides with his current prescription — not from a biobank genotype.

The second output is the one we care about most: every drug that failed a
human ALS trial, split into **never reached the target tissue** versus
**reached it and still failed**. That partition hasn't been published for ALS.

---

## Run it

The expo table binds two ports. FastAPI serves `data/pipeline.json` and live
BBB predict; Vite draws the knowledge graph and proxies `/api`.

```bash
python -m uvicorn server.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8731
cd app && npm install && npm run dev
```

Opens on <http://127.0.0.1:5918>. The graph is the main surface — funnel chips
filter it; clicking a node opens the existing receipt (BBB, descriptors,
ordered filter reasons). `in_domain: false` still shows no probability.

The committed `data/pipeline.json` is the real 3,791-compound merge
(`meta.is_sample: false`). A **"Sample data"** badge only appears if
`merge.py` is pointed at the hand-written sample.

Before pushing:

```bash
npm run check --prefix app     # typecheck + contract tests
```

## How it fits together

Five stages, each removing candidates for a stated reason:

```
4,805 approved drugs
  → linked to ALS biology       (knowledge graph)
  → can reach the target        (blood–brain barrier model)
  → safe and usable for Alex    (patient filter)  ← the contribution
  → not already failed          (trial history)
```

Four Python modules each write one JSON file to `data/`. Nobody imports
anybody else's code — integration happens through files, so all four can be
built at once and a broken module doesn't block the rest. `merge.py` joins
them on InChIKey into `data/pipeline.json`, and the frontend reads that file
and nothing else.

**[`docs/CONTRACT.md`](docs/CONTRACT.md)** is what you need if you're writing
one of those modules. Validate your output without running the frontend:

We need precise, verified facts — not a literature review.

Status: `todo` · `doing` · `blocked` · `done`. Add rows freely; never delete
one that someone else claimed — mark it `done` or `dropped` and say why.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 3 | Real citations for MRgFUS BBB opening in ALS | Henri | doing | `docs/FUS_RESEARCH.md` | The pitch rests on it. |
| 4 | Fix graveyard: undetermined drugs counted as `never_arrived` | Neo | todo | `src/merge.py:211-214`, `contract/contract.ts:88` | See "Found while auditing" #1. Needs a contract change → team. |

| 10 | One FaceCheck, not two | Neo + Levi | todo | `facecheck/` vs `speech-tests-backup/speech_demo/facecheck/` | See #3 below. |
| 11 | Supabase: owner, and demo signed-in or on sample data? | team | todo | `frontend/src/lib/supabase.ts` | Sample data works today with no keys. |
| 12 | Delete merged/stale branches | Henri | todo | remote | `frontend/diagnosis` (merged), `codex/diagnostic-tests` (subset of Master-UI). |

## Branches — every one on the remote

| Branch | Owner | State | What's on it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | all | live | Motus (`frontend/`): landing, overview dashboard, **scripted** discovery pipeline. `contract/`, sample `data/pipeline.json`. |
| `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui` | Neo | live, 20 ahead / 9 behind | Real pipeline: trained BBB model, DRKG TransE ranking, patient filter, graveyard → a real 3,791-compound `pipeline.json`. FastAPI on :8731. Graph UI in `app/`. |
| `cursor/facial-als-validation` | Neo | live, 4 ahead | FaceCheck (`facecheck/`), MediaPipe facial amplitude. Spec: `FACECHECK_SPEC.md`. |
| `Master-UI-Neo-Face-Integration` | Levi | live, unrelated history | Speech + diagnostic tests (`master-app/`, `speech-test-good/`, `facial-test/`, `line-test/`, `SVD-diagnostic/`), plus a JS port of FaceCheck. |
| `codex/diagnostic-tests` | Levi | stale | Same as Master-UI minus its last commit. Safe to delete once Levi confirms. |
| `frontend/kg-and-provenance` | Henri | stale | Knowledge-graph + provenance panels for the deleted `app/`. Port pieces deliberately or drop it. |
| `frontend/diagnosis` | Jeremy | merged | Fully in `main` (PR #2). Safe to delete. |

## Found while auditing — read before you pitch

1. **The graveyard overstates `never_arrived`.** Neo's real `pipeline.json`
   has 24 `never_arrived` / 8 `arrived_failed`. But **21 of the 24 have no BBB
   prediction at all** (biologics, or out of the model's domain) —
   `src/merge.py:211-214` files "no prediction" as `never_arrived`. Only
   ceftriaxone (p 0.39), pentoxifylline (0.29) and pioglitazone (0.29) are
   actually predicted BBB-negative. Honest split: **3 / 8 / 21 undetermined**.
   `bbb/score.py:55` on the same branch already says `undetermined`; the
   contract's two-value enum is what forces the wrong answer. A judge who
   knows gabapentin crosses the BBB, or that tirasemtiv acts on muscle, will
   catch this.
2. **The same thing in the funnel.** "2,440 eliminated: predicted
   BBB-negative" is **1,593 predicted negative + 847 out of domain.** For the
   FUS pitch the honest number is still strong: *1,593 approved drugs the model
   says can't cross.*
3. **Neo's UI can't merge as-is.** It edits `app/`, which `main` deleted at
   23:05 (`3e1a960`). Git will report modify/delete conflicts on every file.
   The Python, `artifacts/` and `data/` merge cleanly in principle; the graph
   UI would have to be ported into `frontend/`.
4. **We have three knowledge graphs and two FaceChecks.** Graph: Neo's
   `GraphCanvas` (`app/`), Henri's `KnowledgeGraph.tsx` (`app/`, stale), and a
   "coming soon" placeholder on `main`. FaceCheck: Neo's TS original and Levi's
   JS port. Pick one of each.
5. **Discovery stage 3 is fake while a real one exists.** `MATCHES` in
   `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts` is hand-written; Neo's `src/drkg.py` loads the
   real DRKG TransE vectors. Note DRKG embeds *entities*, not text — a profile
   has to become DRKG genes before it has a vector. Jeremy's profiles already
   list target genes, so that bridge is short.

## Just landed

- **2026-11-07 23:16** — FUS pitch written down: `DISCOVERY_SPEC.md`.
- **2026-11-07 23:05** — Repo cleanup on `main`: `app/` and `web/` deleted;
  contract extracted to `contract/`; `.gitignore` rewritten (`.env` was not
  ignored); `.workspace/` added; CI repointed.
- **2026-11-07 22:43** — `frontend/` (Motus) merged to `main` via PR #2.

> Names are from git history (Henri = penguinyogurt28, Jeremy = JeremySiu,
> Neo = proneo14, Levi = Levi33k-creator). Correct them if they're wrong.

## Branches — every one on the remote

| Branch | Owner | State | What's on it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | all | live | Motus (`frontend/`): landing, overview dashboard, **scripted** discovery pipeline. `contract/`, sample `data/pipeline.json`. |

| `codex/diagnostic-tests` | Levi | stale | Same as Master-UI minus its last commit. Safe to delete once Levi confirms. |
| `frontend/kg-and-provenance` | Henri | stale | Knowledge-graph + provenance panels for the deleted `app/`. Port pieces deliberately or drop it. |
| `frontend/diagnosis` | Jeremy | merged | Fully in `main` (PR #2). Safe to delete. |

## Found while auditing — read before you pitch

1. **The graveyard overstates `never_arrived`.** Neo's real `pipeline.json`
   has 24 `never_arrived` / 8 `arrived_failed`. But **21 of the 24 have no BBB
   prediction at all** (biologics, or out of the model's domain) —
   `src/merge.py:211-214` files "no prediction" as `never_arrived`. Only
   ceftriaxone (p 0.39), pentoxifylline (0.29) and pioglitazone (0.29) are
   actually predicted BBB-negative. Honest split: **3 / 8 / 21 undetermined**.
   `bbb/score.py:55` on the same branch already says `undetermined`; the
   contract's two-value enum is what forces the wrong answer. A judge who
   knows gabapentin crosses the BBB, or that tirasemtiv acts on muscle, will
   catch this.
2. **The same thing in the funnel.** "2,440 eliminated: predicted
   BBB-negative" is **1,593 predicted negative + 847 out of domain.** For the
   FUS pitch the honest number is still strong: *1,593 approved drugs the model
   says can't cross.*
3. **Neo's UI can't merge as-is.** It edits `app/`, which `main` deleted at
   23:05 (`3e1a960`). Git will report modify/delete conflicts on every file.
   The Python, `artifacts/` and `data/` merge cleanly in principle; the graph
   UI would have to be ported into `frontend/`.
4. **We have three knowledge graphs and two FaceChecks.** Graph: Neo's
   `GraphCanvas` (`app/`), Henri's `KnowledgeGraph.tsx` (`app/`, stale), and a
   "coming soon" placeholder on `main`. FaceCheck: Neo's TS original and Levi's
   JS port. Pick one of each.
5. **Discovery stage 3 is fake while a real one exists.** `MATCHES` in
   `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts` is hand-written; Neo's `src/drkg.py` loads the
   real DRKG TransE vectors. Note DRKG embeds *entities*, not text — a profile
   has to become DRKG genes before it has a vector. Jeremy's profiles already
   list target genes, so that bridge is short.

- **2026-11-07 23:05** — Repo cleanup on `main`: `app/` and `web/` deleted;
  contract extracted to `contract/`; `.gitignore` rewritten (`.env` was not
  ignored); `.workspace/` added; CI repointed.
- **2026-11-07 22:43** — `frontend/` (Motus) merged to `main` via PR #2.

> Names are from git history (Henri = penguinyogurt28, Jeremy = JeremySiu,
> Neo = proneo14, Levi = Levi33k-creator). Correct them if they're wrong.

# Discovery pipeline — FUS-enabled drug repurposing

Owner: Jeremy. Status: **scripted demo built** on `main`
(`frontend/src/components/discovery/`, `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts`).

Recorded 2026-11-07 from Jeremy's pitch, plus what's actually in the code.
Where the two differ, the code wins and this file says so.

---

## 1. The pitch

> The blood–brain barrier was the biggest barrier to drug delivery for ALS.
> With focused-ultrasound MRI from Sunnybrook, we can now look into new drugs
> that couldn't penetrate the BBB that can potentially reduce symptoms,
> develop a cure, or increase life expectancy.

**The move is an inversion.** Every repurposing screen for a CNS disease
treats BBB permeability as a filter and throws away what can't cross. If
MRgFUS can open the barrier focally and temporarily, that discarded set
becomes the interesting one — it has been excluded on a delivery constraint,
not on biology.

This is the strongest framing the project has had, because the thing it
proposes to search is a set nobody has had a reason to search.

### It connects to work already in this repo

`data/pipeline.json` carries a **graveyard partition**: every drug that
failed a human ALS trial, split into

- `never_arrived` — predicted barrier-negative, so it may never have reached
  the tissue at the dose that mattered, and
- `arrived_failed` — predicted barrier-positive, got there, still failed.

**`never_arrived` is, by construction, the candidate pool this pitch is
about.** A drug that failed because it never arrived is the one worth
re-asking under FUS. That partition was built for the old elimination funnel;
it turns out to be the input to the new pipeline. Nobody has to rebuild it.

> Unverified as of this writing: whether the two sets were produced with the
> same BBB model and are directly comparable. Check before claiming it on
> stage.

---

## 2. The pipeline

Jeremy's five stages, as pitched and as coded in `STAGES`:

| # | Stage | What it does | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `analysis` | An agent reads the patient record and derives the characteristics of the ideal drug for *this* person | NCBI, ClinVar, Open Targets |
| 2 | `profiles` | The same agent runs **5× in parallel**, each producing a slightly different ideal-drug profile | — |
| 3 | `embedding` | Each profile → vector in the **DRKG** embedding space → cosine search over compounds | TransE over DRKG |
| 4 | `research` | A research agent with open web search ranks the top matches for this patient | web search |
| 5 | `report` | Cited report: each drug, its effects, and the new potential FUS gives it | — |

Running the profile agent five times is the part worth defending. One agent
gives you one opinion; five give you a spread, and a compound that surfaces
across several profiles is a different kind of hit from one that surfaces
once. Say that out loud in the pitch — it reads as rigour, not as padding.

### Ranking dimensions

Not just biological fit. Each candidate is scored on:

- **Cost** of the drug or treatment
- **Availability** — does it exist in this country, and what do regulations allow
- **User acceptance** — would this patient consent, how standardised is it
- **Safety** — side effects against existing conditions and current medication

Plus, in the code, the pair that carries the whole argument: **`bbbAlone`**
vs **`withFus`** per candidate ("Very low" → "Requires BBB opening";
"Low" → "Motor-cortex delivery plausible"). That column *is* the thesis. It
should be the most visually prominent thing in the report.

---

## 3. What's actually built

`runDemoPipeline` replays **fixed events on timers**. Nothing calls NCBI,
no embedding runs, no agent executes. The UI labels the run "Simulated" and
the module header says every output is illustrative.

This is the right call for a 90-second demo and it should stay — but it
means **the honest claim is "here is the system we designed", not "here is
a system that found these drugs".** The sample patient (`A-0417`, bulbar
onset, 14 months, ALSFRS 38, Toronto/OHIP, `fusEligible: true`) and its
candidates are hand-written.

A live backend only has to emit the same `PipelineEvent`s. That's a clean
seam; don't let anyone collapse it under time pressure.

---

## 4. Open questions — these need people, not agents

1. **Is this the product, or is Motus?** `main` currently ships a landing
   page and a longitudinal monitoring dashboard (speech/typing/handwriting
   vs personal baseline) *and* this discovery pipeline. They share a sidebar
   and nothing else. One demo, 90 seconds — a judge can follow one argument.
   **This is the most important open question in the repo.**
2. **What is it called?** `theme.ts`, `pipeline.ts` and `report.tsx` say
   **Addo Labs**. The landing page says **motus**. Pick one today.
3. **Does the old elimination funnel feed this?** The discovery module is
   self-contained and never reads `data/pipeline.json`. Either wire the
   graveyard in as the candidate pool (§1 — cheap, and it makes the two
   tracks one story) or retire the contract and say so.
4. **Can we cite the Sunnybrook FUS work accurately?** The claim rests on
   it. Get real citations for BBB opening in ALS or in neurodegeneration
   generally, and be precise about what has been shown in humans versus what
   is proposed. Mark anything unverified as unverified — a judge who knows
   the field will ask.
5. **Does FaceCheck still fit?** See `FACECHECK_SPEC.md` §7.

---

## 5. Risks worth naming before a judge does

- **Safety inverts too.** Opening the BBB for a drug also opens it for
  everything else circulating, and the drugs this unlocks were often not
  designed for CNS exposure. "It can now get in" is not "it is now safe
  once it's in." Having an answer here is a strength.
- **The ranking is the claim.** Cosine similarity in DRKG plus an LLM's
  reading is a hypothesis generator, not evidence. Frame the output as "what
  to investigate next", never as a recommendation.
- **Nothing is validated.** Same rule as FaceCheck: say so on every screen.

# BioHacks 2026 — repo guide for humans and AI

**This file is the single source of truth.** `CLAUDE.md` imports it; Codex,
Cursor and Copilot read it directly. If you change how the project works,
change it **here**, not in a second file and not in a DM.

Devpost closes **Sun 2026-11-08 11:30 am**; expo judging 1:30–3:00 pm. Treat
**9:00 am Sunday** as the real deadline and leave the last two hours for the
pitch.

---

## Read this before you touch anything

Four people are working in parallel with AI agents. The thing that has cost
us the most time is not bugs — it is **two people building the same thing
because neither knew what the other was doing.** We have already shipped
three separate frontends for one project.

So, in order, every session:

1. **Read [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md).** It says who is on what, right
   now. It takes fifteen seconds and it is the whole point.
2. **Check the map below** for which directory your work belongs in. If your
   change doesn't obviously fit one, say so before writing code.
3. **Before you stop, update `docs/STATUS.md`.** Even "I got nowhere on X"
   is worth more to the other three than silence.

If you are an agent: do steps 1 and 3 without being asked. Step 3 happens in
the same commit as your work, not as a follow-up you forget.

---

## What's here

| Directory | What it is | Stack |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/` | **Motus** — the product. Longitudinal at-home ALS monitoring: speech, typing and handwriting tracked against a personal baseline. Landing + dashboard. | Vite · React 19 · TS · Tailwind v4 · shadcn/ui · Supabase · three |
| `contract/` | The `data/pipeline.json` schema, its tests, and the CLI validator. Owned by nobody, depended on by everybody. | zod · node:test |
| `data/` | `pipeline.json` — the frozen contract plus a hand-written sample. | — |
| `docs/` | Specs, research, decisions, status. **See "Documentation" below.** | — |
| `.claude/skills/` | 21 pinned design/frontend skills. See `CLAUDE.md`. | — |
| `.workspace/` | Your personal scratch, gitignored. See its README. | — |

### Work that lives on branches, not on main

Not everything is merged. Before starting something, check whether it already
exists here:

| Branch | What's on it |
|---|---|
| `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui` | The **drug-repurposing pipeline** — `bbb_model.py`, `patient_filter.py`, `merge.py`, `graveyard.py`, scored across 3,791 compounds. This is live work, not abandoned. |
| `cursor/facial-als-validation` | **FaceCheck** (`facecheck/`) — MediaPipe facial-amplitude prototype. Spec: [`docs/FACECHECK_SPEC.md`](docs/FACECHECK_SPEC.md). |
| `Master-UI-Neo-Face-Integration` | Speech and diagnostic test apps (`master-app/`, `speech-test-good/`, `facial-test/`, `line-test/`). **Unrelated git history** — it does not share a root with `main`. Merging it is a decision, not a chore; log it in `docs/DECISIONS.md` first. |

**Nothing above is dead.** If you think a track should be dropped, that is a
decision — write it down, don't silently stop maintaining it.

---

## The rules that keep four people from colliding

### One track per branch, one owner per file

Two agents editing the same file in parallel is how we lose an afternoon.
Claim your area in `docs/STATUS.md` and stay in it. If you need a change in
somebody else's file, say so in STATUS rather than reaching in.

### Don't build a second one

Before creating a new app, page, module or script: **search for it first.**
`git branch -r`, then grep. Three frontends happened because nobody looked.
If what exists is wrong, fix or replace it deliberately and say so — don't
leave both standing.

### Integration happens through files, not imports

Each module writes **one JSON file**. Nobody imports anybody else's code.

```
the Python pipeline  → data/pipeline.json   (validated by contract/)
FaceCheck            → facecheck.session.v3 (its own export)
frontend/            → reads what it's given, imports no pipeline code
```

This decoupling is the schedule: all four tracks can be built at once and a
broken module doesn't block the rest. **Do not propose refactors that couple
them.**

### The contract is frozen

`data/pipeline.json`'s executable definition is
[`contract/contract.ts`](contract/contract.ts); the annotated prose version is
[`docs/CONTRACT.md`](docs/CONTRACT.md).

Check your output without running any frontend:

```bash
npm run validate --prefix contract -- path/to/your.json
```

Exits non-zero with readable problems. If the shape genuinely must change:
update `contract/contract.ts`, update the sample in `data/pipeline.json`, run
`npm test --prefix contract`, log it in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, and **tell the
team in the same breath.**

---

## Documentation — what goes in `docs/`

The test is simple: **would a teammate arriving tomorrow need this, and would
they find it?** If yes, it goes in `docs/`. Not in a commit message, not in
chat, not in your head.

| File | What belongs in it | When you write it |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/STATUS.md` | Who is on what, blockers, what just landed. | Start and end of every session. |
| `docs/DECISIONS.md` | Why we chose X over Y. Append-only, newest first. | Any time you make a call someone could reasonably reverse. |
| `docs/CONTRACT.md` | The `pipeline.json` shape, annotated. | When the contract changes. |
| `docs/<THING>_SPEC.md` | A design: what it's for, what exists, what's open. | Before building something non-trivial. |
| `docs/<THING>_RESEARCH.md` | Findings with citations. Mark anything unverified as **unverified** — never guess an author or year. | As you research. |

**Non-trivial work leaves a doc behind.** A spec before, findings after. If
the explanation lives only in a chat window, it does not exist on Sunday
morning when someone else has to demo it.

### Decisions get logged, not argued twice

`docs/DECISIONS.md` entries are three lines: what we decided, why, and what
it rules out. A decision in the log is **settled** — don't re-litigate it
without new information, and if you do reverse one, append the reversal
rather than editing history.

---

## Branches, commits, PRs

- **Branch naming: `<track>/<what>`.** Tracks are `pipeline`, `facecheck`,
  `speech`, `frontend`, `docs`. We currently have four naming conventions in
  flight (`cursor/…`, `codex/…`, `Master-UI-…`); new branches use this one so
  `git branch -r` is readable.
- **Branch per piece of work. PR into `main`.** No direct pushes to `main`.
- **Commit messages say _why_, not what.** The diff already says what.
- **Never leave `main` in a state where the frontend doesn't render.** A
  broken demo costs more than a missing feature.
- Non-trivial logic leaves **one runnable check** behind.
  [`contract/contract.test.ts`](contract/contract.test.ts) is the pattern:
  node's built-in test runner, no framework.

---

## Commands

```bash
npm install --prefix frontend          # once
npm run dev --prefix frontend          # Motus on :5173

npm test     --prefix contract         # contract tests
npm run validate --prefix contract -- <file>   # validate any pipeline JSON
```

CI (`.github/workflows/check.yml`) runs the contract tests and a frontend
typecheck + build on every PR.

---

## Working style

- **Shortest working diff.** No abstraction for one use, no config for a
  value that never changes, no scaffolding "for later".
- Audience: judges at an expo table, 90 seconds, laptop screen. Optimise for
  one legible story at arm's length, not for mobile.
- Colour never carries meaning alone — pair it with a glyph, a shape or a
  position. (Our pass/fail pair measured ΔE 7.9 for deuteranopia.)
- Numbers are tabular. Reason strings render **verbatim** — they're the

content.text:
The tracking doc is [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md), the same one AGENTS.md already tells everyone to read. I added a task board where you claim a row by putting your name in it and pushing. It's on branch `docs/status-board`, but it isn't on main yet. The GitHub CLI isn't installed here, so I couldn't open the PR. You can open it here: https://github.com/penguinyogurt/BioHacks-2026/pull/new/docs/status-board

## Who's on what

| Person | Branch | State |
|---|---|---|
| **Henri** | `main` | Cleaned up the repo, wrote down the FUS pitch (`DISCOVERY_SPEC.md`). Your pitch and its four ranking factors are already in that doc. |
| **Jeremy** | merged to `main` | Motus frontend. The discovery pipeline runs on a timer with hand-written outputs. 15 dashboard views are still "coming soon". |
| **Neo** | `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui` | The real pipeline: a trained BBB model, DRKG ranking, a patient filter and the trial graveyard, scored across 3,791 drugs. Last commit 20:33. |
| **Neo** | `cursor/facial-als-validation` | FaceCheck prototype. |
| **Levi** | `Master-UI-Neo-Face-Integration` | Speech and diagnostic test apps, plus a copy of FaceCheck. Last commit 20:25. |

Three branches weren't tracked anywhere:
- `codex/diagnostic-tests` is an older copy of Levi's branch.
- `frontend/diagnosis` is fully merged.
- `frontend/kg-and-provenance` is yours. It's stale because it targets `app/`, which was deleted.

## What I found that affects the pitch

1. **The trial graveyard overstates `never_arrived`.** It lists 24 failed ALS drugs as never reaching the brain. But 21 of those have no BBB prediction at all; [merge.py:211](src/merge.py) on Neo's branch files "no prediction" there by default. Only 3 are actually predicted not to cross: ceftriaxone, pentoxifylline and pioglitazone. A judge who knows gabapentin crosses the BBB will catch this. Fixing it means adding an `undetermined` bucket to the frozen contract, so it's a team call, then Neo's fix.
2. **The honest headline number is still strong.** "2,440 eliminated as BBB-negative" is really 1,593 predicted negative plus 847 the model won't call. The FUS pool is **1,593 approved drugs**. I put this in `DISCOVERY_SPEC.md`.
3. **Neo's graph UI can't merge.** It edits `app/`, which main deleted at 23:05, so git will report a conflict on every one of those files. His Python and data files can still come over without it.
4. **Two things got built twice or more.** There are three knowledge-graph UIs (Neo's, your stale one, and a placeholder on main) and two FaceChecks (Neo's original and Levi's copy).
5. **Stage 3 of the pitch has a gap.** The DRKG embedding model represents genes, drugs and diseases, not text, so a drug profile written as text has no vector. The fix is short: Jeremy's profiles already list target genes, so average those genes' vectors and compare against the drugs'. Neo already loads these embeddings, which makes stage 3 the one stage we can make real tonight. That's what the question below is asking.

## Still open
- **FUS citation research** is running in the background. It will write `docs/FUS_RESEARCH.md`, which I'll add to the same branch.
- **These need the team, not me:** discovery pipeline or Motus as the product, the name (Addo Labs or motus), whether to add the `undetermined` bucket, and whether to merge Levi's branch.
- **Deleting the merged and stale branches** is on the board too. I'll only do it once you say yes.

  3. **Two live ALS FUS drug trials**: **NCT07193953** (Sunnybrook, phase I, n=6, **active not recruiting**) — IVIg 0.4→0.8 g/kg with one bilateral motor-cortex BBB opening, primaries are safety/feasibility plus NfL; **NCT07571486** "Son-ALS" (AP-HP Paris, phase 1/2a, n=23, **recruiting**) — implanted SonoCloud-4, 9 sonications over 24 weeks, **no drug in phase 1**, phase 2a primary is blood NfL at week 26. NCT03321487 is completed.
  4. **Risks, cited**: window is <24 h (so drug must be circulating at sonication); focal volume is tiny (350 mm³ vs diffuse ALS); opening is non-selective; and FUS+microbubbles induced sterile inflammation in **rats** — HSP70/IL-1/IL-18/TNFα for ~24 h, NF-κB induction, CD68+ macrophages at 6 days, authors comparing it to ischemia/mild TBI (Kovacs, PNAS 2017;114(1):E75-E84, PMC5224365), contested in correspondence.

1	# MRgFUS and the blood–brain barrier — verified citations for the pitch
2	
3	Compiled 2026-11-07 for the Devpost pitch and the expo table. Every citation
4	below was opened and read (PubMed/PMC/Europe PMC records, ClinicalTrials.gov
5	API). Anything not confirmed in a primary source is marked **unverified**.
6	
7	Answers the open question in `DISCOVERY_SPEC.md` §4.4.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## TL;DR for the pitch
12	
13	- **BBB opening over the motor cortex in ALS has been done in humans, and it
14	  is safe and reversible** — 4 patients at Sunnybrook, gadolinium confirmed
15	  opening, normalized within 24 h, no serious adverse events (Abrahao et al.,
16	  *Nat Commun* 2019). **No drug was delivered in that trial.**
17	- **Drug delivery through FUS-opened BBB has been shown in humans in other
18	  diseases** — trastuzumab into HER2+ brain metastases with a measured ~101%
19	  SUVR increase (Meng et al., *Sci Transl Med* 2021), aducanumab in Alzheimer's
20	  (Rezai et al., *NEJM* 2024), recombinant glucocerebrosidase in Parkinson's
21	  (Meng et al., *Mov Disord* 2022). All n = 3–4, phase I.
22	- **ALS drug-delivery trials are now registered and running** — Sunnybrook
23	  IVIg + FUS (NCT07193953, phase I, n = 6, active not recruiting) and Son-ALS
24	  with an implanted SonoCloud-4 (NCT07571486, phase I/2a, n = 23, recruiting).
25	  So the premise is live, not hypothetical — but no efficacy has been shown.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. The Sunnybrook first-in-human ALS trial — verified
30	
31	**Abrahao A, Meng Y, Llinas M, Huang Y, Hamani C, Mainprize T, Aubert I,
32	Heyn C, Black SE, Hynynen K, Lipsman N, Zinman L.** "First-in-human trial of
33	blood-brain barrier opening in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis using MR-guided
34	focused ultrasound." *Nature Communications* 2019;10(1):4373.
35	DOI [10.1038/s41467-019-12426-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-12426-9) ·
36	PMID 31558719 · PMC6763482 · ClinicalTrials.gov **NCT03321487** (completed,
37	sponsor InSightec, enrollment 4).
38	
39	Your recollection was right on author, journal and year. Specifics:
40	
41	| Question | Answer |
42	|---|---|
43	| n patients | **4** (2 women, 2 men; median age 61, range 56–70) |
44	| Target | **Right primary motor cortex (precentral gyrus)**, non-dominant side, contralateral to the weaker limb; arm region in 2, leg region in 2; targets individualized by motor-task fMRI |
45	| Volume | Two targets of 5 × 5 × 7 mm (175 mm³ each, **350 mm³** total); stated design ceiling 1 cm³ |
46	| Sessions | **One procedure per patient**; 1–2 sonication cycles per target, 2–4 cycles total. Repeat dosing discussed only as future work |
47	| Microbubbles | Definity (perflutren lipid), 4 µL/kg per cycle, ≤20 µL/kg total |
48	| Opening confirmed? | **Yes — new gadolinium enhancement on T1 immediately post-sonication in all 4** |
49	| How long open? | Enhancement **normalized by the 24 h MRI** |
50	| Drug delivered? | **No.** Gadolinium was an imaging marker only |
51	| Safety | **No serious adverse events through 60 days.** Mild/moderate: headache (3), one vagal response, scalp pain/bruising, petechial scalp rash, one transient FLAIR hyperintensity resolved by day 30. No hemorrhage, ischemia or gliosis to 30 days. No accelerated ALSFRS-R decline to day 60; no significant MoCA or EEG change, no epileptiform discharges at 30 days |
52	
53	Authors' own limitations: small open-label single-centre; only limb-onset
54	patients with severe target-limb weakness; small targeted volume; contrast
55	assessment qualitative/semi-quantitative; cortical reorganization in ALS
56	complicates functional targeting; trace extravasation cannot be excluded on
57	GRE. Their forward-looking sentence: MRgFUS "can be coupled with promising
58	therapeutics providing a targeted delivery platform in ALS."
59	
60	Companion paper, same cohort/era, worth knowing a judge may raise it:
61	**Meng Y et al.,** "Glymphatics Visualization after Focused Ultrasound-Induced
62	Blood-Brain Barrier Opening in Humans," *Ann Neurol* 2019; PMID 31525269
63	(DOI **unverified** — not shown in the record I read).
64	
65	---
66	
67	## 2. Has a therapeutic actually been delivered across the BBB in humans?
68	
69	Yes — in three neurological/neuro-oncological settings, all phase I, all tiny.
70	
71	**Brain metastases (clearest evidence of delivery).** Meng Y, Reilly RM,
72	Pezo RC, Trudeau M, Sahgal A, Singnurkar A, Perry J, Myrehaug S, Pople CB,
73	Davidson B, Llinas M, Heyn C, Huang Y, Hamani C, Suppiah S, Hynynen K,
74	Lipsman N. "MR-guided focused ultrasound enhances delivery of trastuzumab to
75	Her2-positive brain metastases." *Sci Transl Med* 2021;13(615):eabj4011.
76	DOI [10.1126/scitranslmed.abj4011](https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.abj4011) ·
77	PMID 34644145 · NCT03714243. **4 patients, 20 outpatient treatments.**
78	Radiolabelled-trastuzumab SPECT: SUVR **+101 ± 71%** in treated lesions vs
79	**−18 ± 26%** in control lesions; >20% uptake increase in 87 ± 17% of
80	sonicated voxels (up to +450% voxel-wise); tumour measurements −19 ± 12%.
81	**No treatment-related serious adverse events.**
82	
83	**Alzheimer's.** Rezai AR, D'Haese PF, Finomore V, Carpenter J, Ranjan M,
84	Wilhelmsen K, Mehta RI, Wang P, Najib U, Vieira Ligo Teixeira C, Arsiwala T,
85	Tarabishy A, Tirumalai P, Claassen DO, Hodder S, Haut MW. "Ultrasound
86	Blood-Brain Barrier Opening and Aducanumab in Alzheimer's Disease."
87	*N Engl J Med* 2024;390(1):55–62.
88	DOI [10.1056/NEJMoa2308719](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2308719) ·
89	PMID 38169490. Your recollection verified. **3 participants**, FUS with each
90	of **six monthly aducanumab infusions** over ~6 months; amyloid reduction on
91	¹⁸F-florbetaben PET **"numerically greater in regions treated with focused
92	ultrasound"** than in untreated homologous contralateral regions. The widely
93	quoted **~32% greater reduction at 26 weeks** and the per-participant
94	centiloid drops come from secondary coverage, not from the abstract I could
95	read — the paper itself is paywalled, so those figures are **unverified**;
96	quote only the "numerically greater" wording on stage. Registration is
97	plausibly NCT05469009 (Exablate BBB disruption with standard-of-care mAb,
98	sponsor Ali Rezai, n = 15, active not recruiting, started 2022-07-14) but the
99	link to this publication is **unverified**.
100	
101	**Parkinson's (enzyme).** Meng Y, Pople CB, Huang Y, Jones RM, Ottoy J,
102	Goubran M, Oliveira LM, Davidson B, Lawrence LSP, Lau AZ, Bethune A,
103	Maralani P, Abrahao A, Hamani C, Hynynen K, Kalia SK, Lipsman N, Kalia LV.
104	"Putaminal Recombinant Glucocerebrosidase Delivery with MR-Guided Focused
105	Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease: A Phase I Study." *Mov Disord*
106	2022;37(10):2134–2139.
107	DOI [10.1002/mds.29190](https://doi.org/10.1002/mds.29190) · PMID 36089809.
108	**4 GBA1-mutation patients**, IV recombinant GCase at 15/30/60 IU/kg every
109	2 weeks with putaminal BBB opening. No serious adverse events; transient
110	dyskinesia in 2. Important caveat: **drug concentration in tissue was not
111	measured** — only BBB permeability by DCE-MRI. Exploratory MDS-UPDRS off-med
112	−12% at 6 months (26 ± 9 → 22 ± 6).
113	
114	**Alzheimer's, opening only (no drug).** Lipsman N, Meng Y, Bethune AJ,
115	Huang Y, Lam B, Masellis M, Herrmann N, Heyn C, Aubert I, Boutet A, Smith GS,
116	Hynynen K, Black SE. *Nat Commun* 2018;9(1):2336.
117	DOI [10.1038/s41467-018-04529-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-04529-6) ·
118	PMID 30046032 · PMC6060168 · NCT02986932. **5 patients, two sessions ~1 month
119	apart** (4 of 5 completed both), right superior frontal gyrus white matter,
120	enhancement resolved by 24 h, no SAEs. Useful as the repeated-session
121	precedent.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 3. Registered ALS FUS trials (ClinicalTrials.gov API, queried 2026-11-07)
126	
127	| NCT | What | Status | n |
128	|---|---|---|---|
129	| **NCT03321487** | BBB opening with MRgFUS in ALS (the Abrahao trial; sponsor InSightec) | **Completed** (2018-04-13 → 2023-09-11) | 4 |
130	| **NCT07193953** | "Targeting Neuroinflammation With Enhanced Delivery of **IVIg** to the Motor Cortex Using Next Generation Dome Helmet Focused Ultrasound in ALS," phase I open-label, Sunnybrook | **Active, not recruiting** (started 2025-04-15; primary completion 2026-11-30) | 6 |
131	| **NCT07571486** | **Son-ALS** — repeated transient BBB opening via implanted **SonoCloud-4**, AP-HP Paris, phase 1/2a | **Recruiting** (start 2026-07-15) | 23 |
132	
133	NCT07193953 detail: bilateral primary motor cortex (arm, leg and bulbar
134	regions), IVIg 0.4 g/kg (cohort 1) then 0.8 g/kg (cohort 2) split over two
135	doses, **one BBB-opening procedure** performed with the second dose, Definity
136	microbubbles, 24-week follow-up. Primaries are IVIg safety, microbubble
137	safety, feasibility of bilateral gadolinium enhancement with normalization,
138	and FUS safety (including ≥6-point ALSFRS-R decline by week 8). Secondary:
139	plasma and CSF NfL, plus inflammatory markers.
140	
141	NCT07571486 detail: SonoCloud-4 implanted under local anaesthesia; **9
142	sonications over 24 weeks** (first 2 weeks post-implant, then 8 at 3-week
143	intervals) targeting upper motor neuron area and adjacent SMA; **no
144	concomitant drug in phase 1**; phase 2a primary is change in blood NfL to
145	week 26.
146	
147	**Edaravone + FUS: no such registered trial found.** A query for edaravone
148	AND ultrasound returned nothing relevant. Do not claim one exists.
149	
150	---
151	
152	## 4. Known risks and limits
153	
154	**Duration of opening is short.** Gadolinium enhancement normalized within
155	24 h in both the ALS and the Alzheimer's cohorts — the therapeutic window is
156	hours, so the drug must be circulating at the time of sonication (Abrahao
157	2019; Lipsman 2018, above).
158	
159	**Focal volume is small.** 350 mm³ across two targets in the ALS trial,
160	against a design ceiling of 1 cm³ (Abrahao 2019). ALS is diffuse; covering
161	the motor system is not the same problem as covering one target. (A reported
162	FDA limit of ~40 cc in the Alzheimer's lecanemab phase is **unverified** —
163	secondary source only.)
164	
165	**Repeated sessions: precedent exists but is thin.** Two sessions a month
166	apart in Alzheimer's (Lipsman 2018), 20 treatments across 4 patients in brain
167	metastases (Meng 2021), biweekly dosing in Parkinson's (Meng 2022). In ALS the
168	published trial was **single-session**; repeated opening in ALS is exactly
169	what NCT07193953 and NCT07571486 are testing now.
170	
171	**Opening is not selective — it exposes brain to everything circulating, and
172	may itself provoke inflammation.** Kovacs ZI, Kim S, Jikaria N, Qureshi F,
173	Milo B, Lewis BK, Bresler M, Burks SR, Frank JA. "Disrupting the blood-brain
174	barrier by focused ultrasound induces sterile inflammation." *PNAS*
175	2017;114(1):E75–E84.
176	DOI [10.1073/pnas.1614777114](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1614777114) ·
177	PMID 27994152 · PMC5224365. **Rats** (female Sprague–Dawley): FUS +
178	microbubbles raised HSP70, IL-1, IL-18 and TNFα for ~24 h with NF-κB pathway
179	induction, parenchymal albumin, TUNEL+ neurons, activated astrocytes and
180	microglia, and CD68+ macrophage infiltration at 6 days; the authors compare
181	the response to ischemia or mild TBI and state that further investigation is
182	required before wide clinical implementation. This is an animal result and was
183	contested in correspondence (Kovacs et al., *PNAS* 2017;114(33):E6737–E6738,
184	DOI 10.1073/pnas.1711544114) — present it as the open safety question it is,
185	not as a settled human finding.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## 5. On stage
190	
191	**Honest claim:** "Focal, reversible BBB opening over the motor cortex has
192	been shown safe in four people with ALS at Sunnybrook, and FUS-assisted
193	delivery of real therapeutics — trastuzumab, aducanumab, glucocerebrosidase —
194	has been demonstrated in humans in other diseases, with ALS drug-delivery
195	trials now registered and running; so we built the screen for the drugs that
196	were only ever excluded on delivery."
197	
198	**Must not claim:** that any drug has been delivered to the ALS motor cortex
199	by FUS, that FUS has improved any ALS outcome, that a FUS + edaravone trial
200	exists, or that opening the barrier makes a non-CNS drug safe once it is in.
201

Davidson B, Llinas M, Heyn C, Huang Y, Hamani C, Suppiah S, Hynynen K,
Lipsman N. "MR-guided focused ultrasound enhances delivery of trastuzumab to
Her2-positive brain metastases." *Sci Transl Med* 2021;13(615):eabj4011.
DOI [10.1126/scitranslmed.abj4011](https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.abj4011) ·
PMID 34644145 · NCT03714243. **4 patients, 20 outpatient treatments.**
Radiolabelled-trastuzumab SPECT: SUVR **+101 ± 71%** in treated lesions vs
**−18 ± 26%** in control lesions; >20% uptake increase in 87 ± 17% of
sonicated voxels (up to +450% voxel-wise); tumour measurements −19 ± 12%.
**No treatment-related serious adverse events.**

**Alzheimer's.** Rezai AR, D'Haese PF, Finomore V, Carpenter J, Ranjan M,
Wilhelmsen K, Mehta RI, Wang P, Najib U, Vieira Ligo Teixeira C, Arsiwala T,
Tarabishy A, Tirumalai P, Claassen DO, Hodder S, Haut MW. "Ultrasound
Blood-Brain Barrier Opening and Aducanumab in Alzheimer's Disease."
*N Engl J Med* 2024;390(1):55–62.
DOI [10.1056/NEJMoa2308719](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2308719) ·

¹⁸F-florbetaben PET **"numerically greater in regions treated with focused
ultrasound"** than in untreated homologous contralateral regions. The widely
quoted **~32% greater reduction at 26 weeks** and the per-participant
centiloid drops come from secondary coverage, not from the abstract I could
read — the paper itself is paywalled, so those figures are **unverified**;
quote only the "numerically greater" wording on stage. Registration is
plausibly NCT05469009 (Exablate BBB disruption with standard-of-care mAb,
sponsor Ali Rezai, n = 15, active not recruiting, started 2022-07-14) but the
link to this publication is **unverified**.

**Parkinson's (enzyme).** Meng Y, Pople CB, Huang Y, Jones RM, Ottoy J,
Goubran M, Oliveira LM, Davidson B, Lawrence LSP, Lau AZ, Bethune A,
Maralani P, Abrahao A, Hamani C, Hynynen K, Kalia SK, Lipsman N, Kalia LV.

Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease: A Phase I Study." *Mov Disord*
2022;37(10):2134–2139.
DOI [10.1002/mds.29190](https://doi.org/10.1002/mds.29190) · PMID 36089809.

2 weeks with putaminal BBB opening. No serious adverse events; transient

**Alzheimer's, opening only (no drug).** Lipsman N, Meng Y, Bethune AJ,
Huang Y, Lam B, Masellis M, Herrmann N, Heyn C, Aubert I, Boutet A, Smith GS,
Hynynen K, Black SE. *Nat Commun* 2018;9(1):2336.
DOI [10.1038/s41467-018-04529-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-04529-6) ·
PMID 30046032 · PMC6060168 · NCT02986932. **5 patients, two sessions ~1 month
apart** (4 of 5 completed both), right superior frontal gyrus white matter,
enhancement resolved by 24 h, no SAEs. Useful as the repeated-session
precedent.

---

## 3. Registered ALS FUS trials (ClinicalTrials.gov API, queried 2026-11-07)

| NCT | What | Status | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NCT03321487** | BBB opening with MRgFUS in ALS (the Abrahao trial; sponsor InSightec) | **Completed** (2018-04-13 → 2023-09-11) | 4 |
| **NCT07193953** | "Targeting Neuroinflammation With Enhanced Delivery of **IVIg** to the Motor Cortex Using Next Generation Dome Helmet Focused Ultrasound in ALS," phase I open-label, Sunnybrook | **Active, not recruiting** (started 2025-04-15; primary completion 2026-11-30) | 6 |
| **NCT07571486** | **Son-ALS** — repeated transient BBB opening via implanted **SonoCloud-4**, AP-HP Paris, phase 1/2a | **Recruiting** (start 2026-07-15) | 23 |

NCT07193953 detail: bilateral primary motor cortex (arm, leg and bulbar
regions), IVIg 0.4 g/kg (cohort 1) then 0.8 g/kg (cohort 2) split over two
doses, **one BBB-opening procedure** performed with the second dose, Definity
microbubbles, 24-week follow-up. Primaries are IVIg safety, microbubble
safety, feasibility of bilateral gadolinium enhancement with normalization,
and FUS safety (including ≥6-point ALSFRS-R decline by week 8). Secondary:
plasma and CSF NfL, plus inflammatory markers.

NCT07571486 detail: SonoCloud-4 implanted under local anaesthesia; **9
sonications over 24 weeks** (first 2 weeks post-implant, then 8 at 3-week
intervals) targeting upper motor neuron area and adjacent SMA; **no
concomitant drug in phase 1**; phase 2a primary is change in blood NfL to
week 26.

**Edaravone + FUS: no such registered trial found.** A query for edaravone
AND ultrasound returned nothing relevant. Do not claim one exists.

**Duration of opening is short.** Gadolinium enhancement normalized within
24 h in both the ALS and the Alzheimer's cohorts — the therapeutic window is
hours, so the drug must be circulating at the time of sonication (Abrahao
2019; Lipsman 2018, above).

against a design ceiling of 1 cm³ (Abrahao 2019). ALS is diffuse; covering
the motor system is not the same problem as covering one target. (A reported
FDA limit of ~40 cc in the Alzheimer's lecanemab phase is **unverified** —
secondary source only.)

apart in Alzheimer's (Lipsman 2018), 20 treatments across 4 patients in brain
metastases (Meng 2021), biweekly dosing in Parkinson's (Meng 2022). In ALS the
published trial was **single-session**; repeated opening in ALS is exactly
what NCT07193953 and NCT07571486 are testing now.

**Opening is not selective — it exposes brain to everything circulating, and
may itself provoke inflammation.** Kovacs ZI, Kim S, Jikaria N, Qureshi F,
Milo B, Lewis BK, Bresler M, Burks SR, Frank JA. "Disrupting the blood-brain
barrier by focused ultrasound induces sterile inflammation." *PNAS*
2017;114(1):E75–E84.
DOI [10.1073/pnas.1614777114](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1614777114) ·
PMID 27994152 · PMC5224365. **Rats** (female Sprague–Dawley): FUS +
microbubbles raised HSP70, IL-1, IL-18 and TNFα for ~24 h with NF-κB pathway

microglia, and CD68+ macrophage infiltration at 6 days; the authors compare
the response to ischemia or mild TBI and state that further investigation is
required before wide clinical implementation. This is an animal result and was
contested in correspondence (Kovacs et al., *PNAS* 2017;114(33):E6737–E6738,
DOI 10.1073/pnas.1711544114) — present it as the open safety question it is,
not as a settled human finding.

---

## 5. On stage

**Honest claim:** "Focal, reversible BBB opening over the motor cortex has
been shown safe in four people with ALS at Sunnybrook, and FUS-assisted
delivery of real therapeutics — trastuzumab, aducanumab, glucocerebrosidase —
has been demonstrated in humans in other diseases, with ALS drug-delivery
trials now registered and running; so we built the screen for the drugs that
were only ever excluded on delivery."

**Must not claim:** that any drug has been delivered to the ALS motor cortex
by FUS, that FUS has improved any ALS outcome, that a FUS + edaravone trial
exists, or that opening the barrier makes a non-CNS drug safe once it is in.

20	  (Rezai et al., *NEJM* 2024), recombinant glucocerebrosidase in Parkinson's
21	  (Meng et al., *Mov Disord* 2022). All n = 3–4, phase I.
22	- **ALS drug-delivery trials are now registered and running** — Sunnybrook
23	  IVIg + FUS (NCT07193953, phase I, n = 6, active not recruiting) and Son-ALS
24	  with an implanted SonoCloud-4 (NCT07571486, phase I/2a, n = 23, recruiting).
25	  So the premise is live, not hypothetical — but no efficacy has been shown.
26

# Discovery pipeline — FUS-enabled drug repurposing

Owner: Jeremy. Status: **scripted demo built** on `main`
(`frontend/src/components/discovery/`, `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts`).

Recorded 2026-11-07 from Jeremy's pitch, plus what's actually in the code.
Where the two differ, the code wins and this file says so.

---

## 1. The pitch

> The blood–brain barrier was the biggest barrier to drug delivery for ALS.
> With focused-ultrasound MRI from Sunnybrook, we can now look into new drugs
> that couldn't penetrate the BBB that can potentially reduce symptoms,
> develop a cure, or increase life expectancy.

**The move is an inversion.** Every repurposing screen for a CNS disease
treats BBB permeability as a filter and throws away what can't cross. If
MRgFUS can open the barrier focally and temporarily, that discarded set
becomes the interesting one — it has been excluded on a delivery constraint,
not on biology.

This is the strongest framing the project has had, because the thing it
proposes to search is a set nobody has had a reason to search.

### It connects to work already in this repo

`data/pipeline.json` carries a **graveyard partition**: every drug that
failed a human ALS trial, split into

- `never_arrived` — predicted barrier-negative, so it may never have reached
  the tissue at the dose that mattered, and
- `arrived_failed` — predicted barrier-positive, got there, still failed.

**`never_arrived` is, by construction, the candidate pool this pitch is
about.** A drug that failed because it never arrived is the one worth
re-asking under FUS. That partition was built for the old elimination funnel;
it turns out to be the input to the new pipeline. Nobody has to rebuild it.

> **Checked 2026-11-07 against Neo's real `pipeline.json`
> (`cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`):** same BBB model, so the sets are comparable —
> but the bucket is inflated. 21 of the 24 `never_arrived` drugs have **no BBB
> prediction** (biologics or out of domain) and were filed there by default
> (`src/merge.py:211-214`). Only ceftriaxone, pentoxifylline and pioglitazone
> are predicted BBB-negative. Say "3 predicted never-arrived, 21 we can't
> call" on stage, not "24". The bigger, honest number for this pitch is the
> funnel's: **1,593 of 3,791 approved drugs predicted BBB-negative** (plus 847
> the model declines to call). That is the FUS-unlocked pool.

---

## 2. The pipeline

Jeremy's five stages, as pitched and as coded in `STAGES`:

| # | Stage | What it does | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `analysis` | An agent reads the patient record and derives the characteristics of the ideal drug for *this* person | NCBI, ClinVar, Open Targets |
| 2 | `profiles` | The same agent runs **5× in parallel**, each producing a slightly different ideal-drug profile | — |
| 3 | `embedding` | Each profile → vector in the **DRKG** embedding space → cosine search over compounds | TransE over DRKG |
| 4 | `research` | A research agent with open web search ranks the top matches for this patient | web search |
| 5 | `report` | Cited report: each drug, its effects, and the new potential FUS gives it | — |

**Stage 3 has a gap in the pitch as worded.** "The same embedding model used
in DRKG" is TransE over *entities* — it has no vector for a sentence. A
profile only gets a DRKG vector once it is written as DRKG entities (genes,
mostly). The profiles in `PROFILES` already list target genes, so: map them
to `Gene::<Entrez>` ids, average their vectors, cosine against compound
vectors. Neo's `src/drkg.py` already loads these embeddings.

Running the profile agent five times is the part worth defending. One agent
gives you one opinion; five give you a spread, and a compound that surfaces
across several profiles is a different kind of hit from one that surfaces
once. Say that out loud in the pitch — it reads as rigour, not as padding.

### Ranking dimensions

Not just biological fit. Each candidate is scored on:

- **Cost** of the drug or treatment
- **Availability** — does it exist in this country, and what do regulations allow
- **User acceptance** — would this patient consent, how standardised is it
- **Safety** — side effects against existing conditions and current medication

Plus, in the code, the pair that carries the whole argument: **`bbbAlone`**
vs **`withFus`** per candidate ("Very low" → "Requires BBB opening";
"Low" → "Motor-cortex delivery plausible"). That column *is* the thesis. It
should be the most visually prominent thing in the report.

---

## 3. What's actually built

`runDemoPipeline` replays **fixed events on timers**. Nothing calls NCBI,
no embedding runs, no agent executes. The UI labels the run "Simulated" and
the module header says every output is illustrative.

This is the right call for a 90-second demo and it should stay — but it
means **the honest claim is "here is the system we designed", not "here is
a system that found these drugs".** The sample patient (`A-0417`, bulbar
onset, 14 months, ALSFRS 38, Toronto/OHIP, `fusEligible: true`) and its
candidates are hand-written.

A live backend only has to emit the same `PipelineEvent`s. That's a clean
seam; don't let anyone collapse it under time pressure.

---

## 4. Open questions — these need people, not agents

1. **Is this the product, or is Motus?** `main` currently ships a landing
   page and a longitudinal monitoring dashboard (speech/typing/handwriting
   vs personal baseline) *and* this discovery pipeline. They share a sidebar
   and nothing else. One demo, 90 seconds — a judge can follow one argument.
   **This is the most important open question in the repo.**
2. **What is it called?** `theme.ts`, `pipeline.ts` and `report.tsx` say
   **Addo Labs**. The landing page says **motus**. Pick one today.
3. **Does the old elimination funnel feed this?** The discovery module is
   self-contained and never reads `data/pipeline.json`. Either wire the
   graveyard in as the candidate pool (§1 — cheap, and it makes the two
   tracks one story) or retire the contract and say so.
4. **Can we cite the Sunnybrook FUS work accurately?** The claim rests on
   it. Get real citations for BBB opening in ALS or in neurodegeneration
   generally, and be precise about what has been shown in humans versus what
   is proposed. Mark anything unverified as unverified — a judge who knows
   the field will ask.
5. **Does FaceCheck still fit?** See `FACECHECK_SPEC.md` §7.

---

## 5. Risks worth naming before a judge does

- **Safety inverts too.** Opening the BBB for a drug also opens it for
  everything else circulating, and the drugs this unlocks were often not
  designed for CNS exposure. "It can now get in" is not "it is now safe
  once it's in." Having an answer here is a strength.
- **The ranking is the claim.** Cosine similarity in DRKG plus an LLM's
  reading is a hypothesis generator, not evidence. Frame the output as "what
  to investigate next", never as a recommendation.
- **Nothing is validated.** Same rule as FaceCheck: say so on every screen.

content.text:
The FUS research is done and in [docs/FUS_RESEARCH.md](docs/FUS_RESEARCH.md), on the same `docs/status-board` branch. I checked the three trial numbers on ClinicalTrials.gov and the three key papers on PubMed, and all matched.

**What you can safely say:**
- **Opening the barrier in ALS is proven safe, but only for opening.** Sunnybrook opened it over the motor cortex in 4 ALS patients (Abrahao et al., *Nature Communications* 2019). It closed again within 24 hours, and nobody had a serious side effect. No drug was given in that trial.
- **Getting a drug through has been shown in people, but not in ALS:**
  - trastuzumab into brain tumours: uptake about doubled (*Science Translational Medicine* 2021)
  - aducanumab in Alzheimer's (*NEJM* 2024)
  - an enzyme in Parkinson's (2022)

  Each study had only 3–4 patients.
- **Two ALS trials that pair the barrier opening with treatment are running now.** Sunnybrook is giving IVIg with it (NCT07193953). Paris is testing repeated opening with an implanted device (NCT07571486), with no drug in the first phase.

**What you must not say:**
- that any drug has reached the ALS motor cortex this way
- that it has improved any ALS outcome
- that an edaravone trial with it exists (there isn't one)
- that a drug becomes safe once it's in. A rat study found that opening the barrier itself causes inflammation; that finding is disputed but still open.

Section 5 of the doc has a one-sentence version of the claim ready for the pitch.

To get all of this onto main, open the PR here: https://github.com/penguinyogurt/BioHacks-2026/pull/new/docs/status-board
